title: Secretary of State of South Carolina

context.text: Incumbent Secretary of State Mark Hammond, a Republican, was unopposed in his party's primary; Democrat Jason Belton is the other candidate in the USA TODAY Network candidate guide. The office handles business filings, notaries and charitable-solicitation registration, according to the incumbent's official biography.

candidates.name: Mark Hammond
candidates.ballotNote: Incumbent; his Republican primary was canceled.
candidates.currentRole: South Carolina Secretary of State (since January 2003)

priorities.text: Continue modernizing the office so services are available online, with "transparency and accountability for taxpayers."
Keep enforcing the SC Solicitation of Charitable Funds Act and providing the Annual Angels list of charities and the Give Smart SC app.

record.text: Reports initiating reforms targeting charity and telemarketing abuses, with more than $5.8 million in fines collected, and requesting improvements to the Solicitation of Charitable Funds Act.
Reports facilitating the seizure of over $72 million in counterfeit merchandise, resulting in the arrest of nearly 660 suspects.
Launched Give Smart SC, a free app letting donors look up registered charities and file complaints with the Secretary of State.
Worked with the General Assembly to modernize the Notary Public statute and developed an online electronic-notarization application.

candidates.name: Jason Belton
candidates.currentRole: Vice president, Greater Columbia Central Labor Council

priorities.text: Voter rights and fair elections, and workers' rights.

sources.title: Meet the statewide candidates in South Carolina's 2026 general election
sources.publisher: SC Now (USA TODAY Network South Carolina)

researchNotes: Slate: the SC State Election Commission's interactive candidate lookup could not be read; the two-candidate slate rests on Ballotpedia and the USA TODAY Network candidate guide only (one news source), so it is lower confidence than other races. Belton's campaign site loads only a title with no readable text, and he did not respond to the newspaper guide, so his priorities come from the guide and his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Hammond's record items are the office's own list of accomplishments. No candidate statement on documentary proof of citizenship was found (South Carolina's State Election Commission, not the Secretary of State, administers elections).
